translationRepairs: Compared with those who advance virtue and broaden the Way, who reform custom and shelter the people, these may seem small and can be overlooked.
Compared with those who advance virtue and broaden the Way, who reform custom and shelter the people, these may seem small and cannot be dismissed.

s0022 contrasts 可得而小 with 不可得而忽也: they may be counted small, but cannot be overlooked. The literal before flips the negation to “can be overlooked”; the proposed “cannot be dismissed” matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.

In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he suddenly fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered a litter to send him back to the mountains. He took up residence at Songgao Daode Temple and died within days.

In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he suddenly fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered a litter to send him back to the mountains. He took up residence at Songgao Daochang Temple and died within days.
s0081 has 嵩高道場寺. 道場 is Daochang (ritual precinct), not 道德/Daode; replacing Daode with Daochang corrects the temple name.
In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he suddenly fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered a litter to send him back to the mountains. He resided at Songgao Daode Temple and died within days.

In the winter of the second year of Yanchang he suddenly fell gravely ill; Emperor Xuanwu ordered a litter to send him back to the mountains. He resided at Songgao Daochang Temple and died within days.
The literal field has the same misreading of 道場 as Daode; Songgao Daochang Temple correctly renders 嵩高道場寺.
At that time the Shouyang Daoist Huixu went each dawn to look upon the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.
At that time the Shouchun Daoist Huixu went each dawn to look upon the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.
s0085 names 壽春道人惠需. 壽春 is Shouchun; Shouyang (壽陽) is a different place-name, so the proposed correction is required.
At that time the Shouyang Daoist Huixu each dawn went to look upon the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.
At that time the Shouchun Daoist Huixu each dawn went to look upon the corpse and brushed away dust and snow.
The literal likewise misreads 壽春 as Shouyang; Shouchun is the correct reading of the place-name.

The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin to expand it into six hundred volumes.
s0174 names 許善心. Standard pinyin is Xu Shanxin (善 shàn, 心 xīn); Xu Shansin misreads 心 and must be corrected.
The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shansin to expand it into six hundred volumes.
The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin to expand it into six hundred volumes.
The literal field repeats Xu Shansin for 許善心; Xu Shanxin is the accurate romanization.
The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand bolts of funeral goods, dispatched a painter to depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Yan to compose a eulogy.
The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand bolts of funeral goods, dispatched a painter to depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bi to compose a eulogy.

Chapter text has the rare-glyph placeholder 柳{巧言}; CText and parallel editions read 柳䛒, the same Liu Bi named earlier in the chapter. Liu Yan is a misreading of that glyph, so Liu Bi is the correct repair.
When a neighbor built a wall with an inward bend in his heart, Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to accommodate him.
When a neighbor built a wall that was not straight, Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to accommodate him.

心有不直 concerns the wall’s alignment (not straight / encroaching), not a figurative bend in the neighbor’s heart. The proposed parenthetical “(encroaching)” is awkward; a plain “not straight” keeps the literal sense while matching the idiomatic.
